findings.statement: a criterion whose PARENT evidence proves nothing (DEPENDENCY_UNRUNNABLE, NOT_COLLECTED, COLLECTION_ABORTED, ABSENT) makes the nop check UNRUNNABLE with failure owner ENVIRONMENT — correct — but the attempt is still charged to the DEVELOPER's quality budget and the story terminates as QUALITY_BLOCK, as though the code had failed
findings.measured: TDD-POLICY-V2-CONFORMANCE.json scenarios G and H on tree 42a29853: check outcome UNRUNNABLE, every blocking row owner=ENVIRONMENT, developer sessions 2, quality attempts 2, terminal QUALITY_BLOCK. The PLAN owner IS routed correctly in the same suite (scenarios B and J: terminal PLAN_CONFLICT, 1 developer session, no retry spent)
findings.impact_in_this_run: none on correctness — fail-closed, 0 false PASS; costs one developer retry and mislabels the terminal
findings.worst_case: a story blocked by an environment that cannot answer is reported as a developer quality failure, and one retry of the model's budget is spent on a condition no code change can fix
findings.why_not_fixed_now: the owner decision of 2026-09-20 specifies retry routing for the PLAN owner only (section 12: 'Do not spend developer retry budget on a planning contradiction'). Routing the ENVIRONMENT owner is an extension of the approved semantics, not a defect against them, and the behaviour predates policy V2 — V2 only gave the condition a name. Section 22 asks for no scope creep; the kernel is frozen for qualification
findings.disposition: P2 backlog — owner decision needed on whether an ENVIRONMENT-owned criterion may consume a developer quality attempt
